name: Aditya Vision Ltd
tagline: Bihar-dominant electronics retailer with a genuinely sustained ~29%/42% 5yr sales/PAT CAGR, now expanding into MP/WB/Chhattisgarh — but ~55x P/E and a promoter sell-down (53%->47%) temper the case
business_overview: Aditya Vision is an electronics/appliance retail chain dominant in Bihar (~50% market share, fully penetrated), expanding into Jharkhand (~85% penetrated) and Uttar Pradesh (~30% penetrated, the largest remaining growth runway given UP's 200M+ population). It targeted 200+ stores by FY26 (207 reached) and continues opening ~30+ stores/year.
fundamentals_table: 5yr sales CAGR ~29%, 5yr PAT CAGR ~42%; FY26 +18% (soft), Q1FY27 +27% / PAT +40%
Borrowings ~Rs 573 Cr (Mar-26), working-capital funded; D/E ~0.8x; CFO turned +Rs 75 Cr TTM
47.14% (Mar-26), down from ~53% a year ago / ~20 pts over 3yr; no pledge
210 at 30-Jun-2026; 30+/yr; entering MP, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh in FY27
fundamentals_narrative: Aditya Vision's fundamentals are strong on a sustained trailing basis, not just a recent inflection: 5yr sales CAGR ~29%, 5yr PAT CAGR ~42%, 5yr avg ROE ~25% (latest ROE 19%, ROCE 17%). FY26 was a soft year (revenue Rs 2,672 Cr +18%, PAT Rs 117 Cr +11%, EBITDA margin 8.5%) after a prolonged monsoon and weak summer hit H1. Q1FY27 reaccelerated hard — revenue Rs 1,193 Cr (+27%; volume +17%, ASP +8%), SSSG 18%, gross margin 16.1% (+75 bps), EBITDA Rs 124 Cr (10.4%, +90 bps), PAT Rs 77 Cr (+40%) — and notably did so despite a mild Eastern-India summer, evidence the store-expansion + SSSG engine works without perfect weather. It remains a working-capital-funded model (borrowings ~Rs 573 Cr, CFO only recently turned positive) and AC is ~42% of sales. Valuation is rich at ~55x P/E / ~11x book, and promoter holding has fallen from ~53% to 47.1% in a year (Chairman sold ~Rs 300 Cr in Sep-2025).
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass; 52-week range Rs 328-598, near the top.
sentiment_summary: Long-running, highly active thread with strong FII/DII participation (SmallCap World Fund and American Funds Insurance Series invested via a Rs 282 Cr preferential allotment in Jan 2024). Business is explicitly, heavily weather-dependent — management itself noted Q1 alone contributes ~40% of annual sales and ~50% of annual profit, with room ACs half of Q1 sales — making the stock highly sensitive to summer-heat forecasts each year, a pattern the community tracks closely and sometimes trades around. A 2024 UP GST raid on warehouses was resolved within days (seizure order cancelled) without lasting impact.
community_signal: Multiple posters (Vivek_6954 among them) track this closely; one detailed comparison (Ajit.ku.agrawal, 2024) found AVL has structurally higher gross and EBITDA margins than peers (including Electronics Mart) due to lower Tier-2/3 rental costs and a high-street-location strategy versus mall-based competitors.

trusted_signals.note: "Solid set of nos from AVL Aditya Vision ltd. prospects still look bright. discl- invested and biased" (post #1152) — a positive, moderate-conviction call. Source of this stock's trusted-thread queueing.

bse_notes: No red-flag corporate actions found. A 2024 UP State GST enforcement action temporarily seized 7 warehouses/prohibited 3 stores; the order was cancelled within days and operations returned to normal. Some community concern (2024) was raised over promoter-family (Sinha) share sales, though not escalated to any regulatory finding.
bull_case: Genuinely sustained fundamentals — 5yr sales CAGR ~29%, PAT CAGR ~42%, 5yr avg ROE ~25% — a multi-year execution record, not a one-quarter story
Q1FY27 grew revenue +27% and PAT +40% DESPITE a mild Eastern-India summer — the SSSG (18%) + ~30 stores/yr engine is working independent of weather

Growth runway widening: UP still only 16% of revenue, and FY27 adds three new states — MP (6-10 stores), West Bengal (6-10), Chhattisgarh (10-12); management says new-state entry has not historically diluted margins
Structurally superior store economics vs peers (low Tier-2/3 rents, high-street locations); gross margin guided up to 15-16% on OEM price hikes; EBITDA margin guidance 8-10% reaffirmed
Institutions (Axis MF, Motilal Oswal MF, Capital Group funds) have been buyers; no promoter pledge
bear_case: Very rich valuation — ~55x P/E, ~11.3x book — leaves no room for a weak-summer quarter or a guidance wobble
Promoter holding fell from ~53% to 47.1% in a year (Chairman offloaded ~Rs 300 Cr in Sep-2025), down ~20 points over three years — insiders reducing into strength is a live confidence question
Heavily seasonal and AC-concentrated (Q1 ~40% of annual sales/~50% of profit; AC ~42% of Q1 sales) — a cool summer directly hits the year, as FY26 H1 showed
Working-capital-funded model: borrowings ~Rs 573 Cr, CFO only just turned positive (Rs 75 Cr TTM after negative prior year); screener flags possible interest-cost capitalisation
Bihar (72% of revenue) exposed to local disruptions — Q1FY27 saw cautious sentiment on LPG/fuel-supply concerns
verdict_headline: The strongest sustained-execution story available — real 5yr compounding, now with a widening multi-state runway — but ~55x P/E and a promoter sell-down keep it a quality compounder, not a 10x-in-2-3-years bet
verdict_reasoning: Trailing numbers are genuinely strong and multi-year (sales CAGR ~29%, PAT CAGR ~42%, ROE ~25%) — this is real execution, not a methodology artefact
Q1FY27 (+27% rev, +40% PAT despite a mild summer) partly de-risks the weather worry and shows the store + SSSG engine compounding on its own
New-state expansion (MP, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh) extends the runway beyond the core Bihar/Jharkhand/UP
But at ~55x P/E / ~11x book, a ~25-30% earnings CAGR only doubles profit every ~3 years with no multiple help — that is a compounder, not a 10x-in-2-3-years path; thesis_fit moved to neither
The promoter sell-down (53%->47% in a year, Chairman Rs 300 Cr block) is the key new watch item; conviction held at Medium-High on execution strength, but finely balanced

open_questions: Why is the promoter group (and Chairman personally) reducing into strength — pure diversification or a view on valuation?
Do the new states (MP/WB/CG) ramp at the unit economics of the core markets, or dilute returns during the build-out?
Does CFO stay positive as ~30 stores/yr keep consuming working capital, or was the TTM turn a one-off inventory drawdown?
How much of the ~55x multiple survives a genuinely weak summer quarter?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium-High (held). Q1FY27 strength despite a mild summer partly de-risks the weather thesis and the multi-state expansion widens the runway (both positive); offset by a new promoter sell-down (53%->47%) and a ~55x P/E that leaves no margin for error. Net roughly neutral; thesis_fit cut to neither on valuation-vs-growth math.

value_chain.theme: organised electronics/appliance retail in eastern/central India Tier 2-3
value_chain.position: regional category-killer — ~50% share in Bihar, expanding into Jharkhand, UP, and now MP/WB/Chhattisgarh; low-rent high-street format
value_chain.bottleneck_node: store rollout pace + local supply-chain/warehousing in each new state
value_chain.note: Organised retail is still taking share from unorganised dealers in these geographies; AVL's rent advantage and first-mover density give real pricing/economics edge — a consolidating supply side that favours the incumbent scaler.

earnings_quality.normalised_note: EBITDA margin ~8.5-9% is the through-cycle level and management guides 8-10%; Q1's 10.4% is normal seasonal peak (Q1 is the summer quarter). No structural peak-margin risk — retail margins are range-bound.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: YoY revenue growth oldest->newest ~ H1FY26 +10% (monsoon-hit), Q3FY26 mid-teens, Q4FY26 +28%, Q1FY27 +27% — dipped in FY26 then reaccelerated to high-20s on SSSG ~18% + ~30 stores/yr; long-term target 20-25%
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~55x trailing needs ~30-35% EPS CAGR FY26-28 at a 25-28x exit; delivered/guided ~24-27% revenue and ~25-30% PAT growth is close but modestly short, so the multiple runs slightly ahead of the rate of change

management_quality.capital_allocation: Reinvests operating cash into new stores at high incremental returns (5yr ROE ~25%); no unrelated diversification; funds working capital partly with debt (~Rs 573 Cr borrowings)
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Geographic laddering — Bihar -> Jharkhand -> UP -> MP/WB/Chhattisgarh; format and category discipline consistent across states

four_box.note: Structural Tier2/3 organized-retail tailwind, ~50% Bihar-share moat, and geographic runway (MP/WB/Chhattisgarh) score well, but market_expectation shows price already implies 30-35% CAGR vs delivered ~24-27% (gap -12%, over-optimistic) — valuation no.
